title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS2 likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs, session IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different sessions.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location data
description: Location history data contains combinations of attributes (timestamps, locations, movement patterns) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals when combined with other information.

title: Profiling an individual through movement patterns
description: The analytics service derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their behavioral data and patterns.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The data store contains and provides identified location history data that is processed by the analytics service to derive patterns about individuals.

title: Location data contains unique references to identity
description: Location history data likely contains unique references (user identifiers, device identifiers) that directly identify the data subject.

title: Location data reveals identifying attributes
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes (home location, workplace, frequent locations, movement patterns) that support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive location data collected beyond functional need
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected and processed more extensively than strictly required for the analytics functionality.

title: Fine-grained location data granularity
description: Location history data is processed at a fine-grained level (session-level, timestamp-level) that may be more detailed than needed for deriving daily routine patterns.

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: Location history is queried 'across sessions' suggesting an excessive amount of personal data is processed beyond what is functionally needed for pattern derivation.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: The analytics service performs additional treatment, analysis, and enrichment of location data to derive daily routine and movement patterns, which may not be necessary for the stated functionality.

title: Data propagation to analytics service
description: Location history data is propagated from the data store to the analytics service where it may be accessible by parties beyond the original collection scope.

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried across sessions and analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Lack of control over location data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location history is processed, analyzed, and what patterns are derived.

title: Lack of control over rectification and erasure of location data
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect location data or remove location history that is no longer relevant for pattern analysis.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history across multiple sessions to derive detailed movement patterns may process more personal data than actually needed for the stated functionality.

title: Lawfulness problems with automated decision making
description: Automated derivation of daily routine and movement patterns from location history may constitute automated decision making that requires specific lawful grounds and may involve sensitive personal data.

title: Sensitive health data disclosed beyond functional necessity
description: Health analytics service returns inferred health-condition risk indicators and trend flags to the companion app. Health data is highly sensitive and may be more sensitive than functionally required for the app's basic functionality.

title: Health data propagated to mobile app where not strictly needed
description: Inferred health insights are propagated from the analytics service to the companion mobile app. The app may not need this level of detailed health data for its core functionality, creating unnecessary exposure.

title: Health data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Personal health data is made accessible to the companion mobile app, which is a predetermined party. This expands the exposure of sensitive health information beyond the analytics service.

title: Profiling individual through health data analysis
description: The analytics service profiles individuals by analyzing health data patterns to generate risk indicators and trend flags. This profiling can link data to specific individuals based on their health behaviors and conditions.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in health analytics
description: Health analytics may combine multiple attributes (e.g., age, location, health metrics) that serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data to specific individuals even without explicit identifiers.

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The analytics service processes identified health data to generate risk indicators and trend summaries. The data subjects are identifiable through their health records.

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed
description: Health-condition risk indicators and trend flags are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject. These attributes can reveal sensitive health conditions.

title: Data subject unawareness of health data processing
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their health data is being processed to generate analytics insights and that this data is being transmitted to the companion app.

title: Lack of data subject control over health data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their health data is processed, what preferences they can set, or how long the data is retained for analytics purposes.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal health data is processed than is actually needed for the analytics functionality. Health risk indicators and trend flags may be more granular than required.

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: Health analytics involves automated decision-making based on sensitive personal data (health conditions), which may raise lawfulness concerns under GDPR and other regulations.
